subject: Post-demo: pricing follow-up + cache-hit model for FintechCo
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@fintech.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + next asks (pricing & caching)

Hi Tom / Ella —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — really helpful to hear how your support flows and the common prompts your agents hit. Quick recap and a few concrete asks to get us to a firm pricing recommendation: 

Recap (very condensed)
- Goals: low-latency assistant for customer support, multi-tenant routing by brand, <10% SLA tail for 95th percentile.
- Expected usage pattern: mix of short templated prompts (status checks, account lookups) and longer summarization prompts (multi-turn).
- Main ask from FintechCo: target effective price in the ballpark you shared on the call so budget can be modeled.

Concrete asks / next steps for pricing model:
1) Please confirm monthly raw token volume expectations (range is fine) and expected monthly unique users. You mentioned a growth profile; a best guess for months 1/6/12 would help.
2) Confirm budget target expressed on the call. Ella, I heard ~$600 per 1M user tokens — please confirm if that’s target or hard cap.
3) Share a short sample (CSV or exported traces) of 200–500 distinct prompts (anonymized) so we can estimate cacheability. If you prefer, we can accept a small set of representative examples pasted into a doc.

Why the sample matters: our hosted billing charges based on billable tokens (tokens the model must compute). If a prompt is served from Redwood prefix/KV cache we won’t re-run inference for repeated prefixes and that reduces billable tokens. The effective $/1M user tokens is roughly base_price_per_1M * (1 - hit_rate). We can run a quick estimate from your sample.

I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a small worksheet we use to show hit-rate sensitivity — will fill after we get your examples.

Proposed next step: you share the sample traces + confirm monthly volume/budget and we’ll turn around a short pricing note (2–3 pages) with pilots and committed tiers.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side:
- Volume: We're expecting approx 800M user tokens/month at launch (month 1), 2.5B by month 6, and ~5B by month 12 in a high-adoption scenario. These are rough but should be fine for modeling.
- Budget target: yes, roughly $600 per 1M user tokens is what our finance leader flagged as the preferred target. Not an absolute hard cap but an internal planning figure.
- Prompts: I’ll export ~400 anonymized prompt samples and drop them in the shared drive link by EOD today.

One question: when you say 'hit rate', are you assuming exact-string prefix matches only? Our prompts include dynamic tokens (account ids) so I want to understand what you consider cacheable.

Tom Hargreaves

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@fintech.co>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next asks (pricing & caching)

Tom —

Great Q. Quick clarification on caching assumptions and a short worked example so we can align expectations before digging into your traces.

1) What Redwood counts as billable tokens
- Billable tokens = tokens the inference engine actually computes for a request. If we can serve a response entirely from a cached KV/prefix entry we do not bill model compute tokens for those responses. Partial cache hits are billed for the tokens we still compute (e.g., suffix generation).

2) Cache mechanics in brief
- Prefix cache: we detect repeated prompt prefixes (template text or repeated system instructions) and serve cached KV-decoded outputs when identical.
- Template extraction: we can normalize out account-specific fields if you provide templating rules; that increases effective hit rate.

3) Back-of-envelope: effective $/1M user tokens = base_price_per_1M * (1 - hit_rate)
- Example assumptions (hosted API pricing illustration only): base_price_per_1M = $1,200 per 1M billable tokens (our uncommitted list price for this model class);
  - If hit_rate = 0% => effective cost = $1,200 per 1M user tokens
  - If hit_rate = 30% => effective cost = $1,200 * (1 - 0.30) = $840 per 1M user tokens
  - If hit_rate = 60% => effective cost = $1,200 * (1 - 0.60) = $480 per 1M user tokens

Interpretation: your $600 target is reachable with ~50%+ effective hit rate at the listed base price, or at lower hit rates if we take a committed/reserved capacity discount (Dedicated).

4) Where variability comes from
- Prompt diversity: many short templated prompts (e.g., "What is my balance?") are high-hitrate; long bespoke prompts (document summarization) are low-hitrate.
- Normalization rules: removing PII/account numbers increases hit rates substantially.
- Session locality: repeated queries in short windows increase reuse of KV cache.

5) Next steps we recommend before a firm quote
- You share the 400 prompts (thanks) so we can run an automated cacheability pass and return an expected hit-rate distribution (p50/p90).
- We'll propose two commercial paths: 1) Hosted with a volume-based tier and a hit-rate sensitivity sheet; 2) Dedicated reserved capacity with a lower base_price_per_1M and a 90/10 split for capacity commitments vs overage economics.

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min slot once we have the prompt samples to walk through the numbers.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@fintech.co>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ella Nguyen <ella@fintech.co>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next asks (pricing & caching)

Marissa / Rafael —

Thanks for the worked examples and explanation, that clears a lot up. A couple quick clarifications:
- The $1,200 base you used is just an illustration, right? We understand list prices vary by model; we mainly wanted to know whether our $600 target is realistic with caching and/or committed discounts.
- On normalization: we can provide templating rules for the top 80% of prompts; account IDs and some URIs are predictable and can be redacted or tokenized before sending. Expect the prompt sample file by EOD.

Assuming we can show a 50%+ hit rate on the initial sample, what would the next pricing step look like? Promo pilot? discount tiers?

Tom

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@fintech.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next asks (pricing & caching)

Thanks Tom — appreciate the quick turnaround. Short answers and proposed timeline: 

1) Base price callout: yes, Marissa used a hosted-list illustrative base ($1,200/1M) to show sensitivity. Actual base depends on model choice and commitment. Dedicated/reserved pricing can materially lower that base (we’ll include examples).

2) If your sample shows ~50% hit rate (or higher) we can model to your $600 target either by:
   - Hosted: show that effective $/1M = base * (1 - hit_rate). If the math doesn’t hit $600, we can layer a modest committed-volume discount to bridge the gap for months 1–12.
   - Dedicated: propose a reserved capacity band that reduces base_price_per_1M; combined with caching it should comfortably land below $600 in many scenarios.

3) Proposed next steps and timeline (we can move quickly):
   - EOD today: you upload the prompt sample.
   - By EOD tomorrow: Redwood runs automated cacheability analysis and returns p50/p90 hit-rate estimates + a short pricing sensitivity sheet (we’ll attach cache-hit-model.xlsx).
   - Day +3: 30-min alignment call to review results and pick a path (pilot hosted vs dedicated pilot).

4) Pilot suggestion (minimal friction)
   - 2-week pilot on Hosted with traffic mirror of a small subset (~5% of production traffic) to measure live hit rates and latency; we’ll instrument cost breakdowns at token-level so you get true end-to-end effective $/1M metrics.

I’ll lock a slot for the Day +3 call once your sample is in. Thanks again — look forward to the samples.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
